headline: An Israeli security startup says Alibaba's free Qwen AI model dodges questions or gives government-friendly answers on topics that China's authorities dislike.
score_reason: Pool score kept: the story matches the headline and CBS ran its own checks, but the main numbers come from one company that has its own fix to promote.
importance_line: Companies and users who build on free Chinese AI models, including U.S. firms such as Uber Eats and Airbnb that have said they use Qwen, could pass political filtering on to their own customers, but the main figures come from one startup that has its own edited version, and Alibaba has not replied.
summary: CBS News reports that Hirundo, an Israeli cybersecurity startup, says Alibaba's free Qwen AI model, which has been downloaded more than 3 billion times, avoids or slants answers on topics the Chinese government dislikes; in CBS's own tests Qwen denied that forced labor camps for Uyghurs exist and often refused questions about the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests. Hirundo, which has made its own edited "Westernized" version, says the original gave censored or biased answers to 89.8% of sensitive political prompts, and Alibaba did not respond to CBS.
notes: Hirundo's 89.8% and 2.8% figures are the company's own and were not independently checked in the article.
